Area.evidence_source: One characteristic of the non-attempters in the current study was their active efforts to develop effective coping strategies. Carver (1998) outlined how positive coping involves ". . . problem focussed coping, positive reframing, and even acceptance of the reality of the existence of a problem . . . (p. 261). Sam demonstrates these traits in his quest to bolster self-esteem through the compilation of a list of L/B/G role models: Leon's strategy similarly involved problem focussed coping; he actively strengthened his social support network to secure self-esteem:
